chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yaqub ibn Yazeed, from Zakariyya al-Khazzaz, from Yahya al-Hadhdha', who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Sometimes I buy something in the presence of my father, so I see from him what saddens me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Avoid it and do not buy in his presence. So when you have a right upon a man, say to him, 'Let him write it,' and let so-and-so write it in his own handwriting, and call Allah as witness upon himself, and suffice with Allah as Witness, for he will fulfill it during his lifetime or after his death.'

key_terms.أَغْتَمُّ بِهِ: I am saddened by it / regret it
key_terms.بِحَضْرَةِ أَبِي: in the presence of my father

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended procedure for securing a financial right or debt according to Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical jurisprudence of debt collection, advising the avoidance of informal transactions with one's father to prevent emotional regret, while emphasizing the spiritual weight of invoking Allah as a witness in written contracts. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on preserving family harmony through clear, documented rights that remain enforceable even after death, reflecting the broader Islamic legal principle of securing financial obligations through tangible evidence.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Zakariyya Al Khazzaz, from Yahya Al Haza’a who said,

‘I said to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Sometimes I buy the thing in the presence of my father, so I see from him what I get saddened with’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Avoid him and do not buy in his presence. So when there was a right for you upon a man, so say to him, ‘So let us write (an agreement)’, and let so and so write in his own handwriting, and keeps Allah<sup>azwj</sup> as a witness upon himself and suffice with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> as a Witness, for he would fulfil it during his lifetime or after his death’.
en.sarwar: 54. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from Mus‘ab ibn ‘Abd Allah al- Nawfaliy from the one who has narrated in a marfu’ manner who has said the following:

“Once an Arab came on his camel in the time of the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and said, ‘O Messenger of Allah, sell my (herd of) camels for me.’ The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, said, ‘I am not a camel seller in the market.’ He then said, ‘Give me an idea.’ The Messenger of Allah said, ‘Sell this he-camel for so and so much and this she-camel for so and so much until he (the Messenger of Allah) explained for him about every camel there. The Arab man went to the market and sold them. He then came back to the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, and said, ‘I swear by the One who has sent you with truth, not one dirham was less or more than what you had said it was, so accept my gift, O Messenger of Allah.’ He (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘No, I do not accept.’ He said, ‘Yes, O Messenger of Allah, accept it.’ They continued speaking until he (the Messenger of Allah) said, ‘You must give us a she-camel as a gift and you must not separate it from its young.’”
